response.sql: WITH filtered_films AS (SELECT f.rating, f.rental_rate, f.rental_duration, f.rental_rate / f.rental_duration AS rate_per_day FROM film f WHERE f.rental_duration >= 5), rating_stats AS (SELECT rating, AVG(rate_per_day) AS avg_rate_per_day, COUNT(*) AS film_count FROM filtered_films GROUP BY rating), benchmark AS (SELECT AVG(avg_rate_per_day) AS benchmark_value FROM rating_stats) SELECT rs.rating, rs.avg_rate_per_day, rs.film_count, rs.avg_rate_per_day / b.benchmark_value FROM rating_stats rs CROSS JOIN benchmark b WHERE b.benchmark_value IS NOT NULL;

assumptions.assumption: The metric is the average of (rental_rate / rental_duration) for each film, computed as AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration), not AVG(rental_rate) / AVG(rental_duration). The phrase '(ignoring missing values)' suggests per-film calculations are averaged, supporting this interpretation.

alternatives.interpretation: The metric for each rating is the ratio of aggregate averages: AVG(rental_rate) / AVG(rental_duration), interpreting 'average of X divided by Y' as (average of X) divided by (average of Y).
alternatives.sql: WITH filtered_films AS (SELECT f.rating, f.rental_rate, f.rental_duration FROM film f WHERE f.rental_duration >= 5), rating_stats AS (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate) / AVG(rental_duration) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(*) AS film_count FROM filtered_films GROUP BY rating), benchmark AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS benchmark_value FROM rating_stats) SELECT rs.rating, rs.avg_ratio, rs.film_count, rs.avg_ratio / b.benchmark_value FROM rating_stats rs CROSS JOIN benchmark b WHERE b.benchmark_value IS NOT NULL;
